subject: Post-call recap: spend runway, token-melt & batching hypotheses
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@cashlance.com>, CashLance Procurement <procurement@cashlance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: spend runway, token-melt & batching hypotheses

Asha — thanks for your time this morning. Quick written recap so we have aligned next steps and the cost hypotheses to validate during a pilot.

Summary of customer pain / goals from the call
- Primary constraint: inference budget capped ~ $60k / month for production inference (all channels).
- Product goal: ship a multi-turn customer support assistant with SLA ~500ms median latency; batching/throughput can be used for background jobs, but interactive flows must stay snappy.
- Current architecture: internal service endpoints generate ~1.2M tokens/day based on expected traffic in Q3 (peaks at ~1.8M tokens/day).

Top cost levers we discussed (initial hypotheses & conservative estimates)
1) Workload-aware batching (micro-batching window, 5–20ms): estimated token cost reduction 30–40% for background workflows; expected 8–12% impact on interactive median latency in peak windows.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated flows (help-center templates & top-20 intents): estimated 18–28% effective token reduction on those conversational paths; hit-rate depends on reuse of canned system prompts.
3) Model quantization & variant routing: heavy quantization (4-bit) for low-risk paths -> ~20–30% unit cost reduction; route high-criticality flows to fp16.
4) Dedicated capacity commit (12-month or 3-month pilot credit): hosted per-token baseline ~ $0.032/token for the chosen open model; projected dedicated blended rate after commit ~ $0.018–0.022/token.

Quick ROI framing (conservative example)
- Baseline: 1.2M tokens/day * 30 days = 36M tokens/mo. At $0.032/token = $1,152,000/mo (this is illustrative — we used high-touch assumptions to show sensitivity).
- With batching + caching + routing (combined conservative delta ~45%): 36M * 0.55 = 19.8M tokens/mo -> at $0.022/token (dedicated blend) = $435,600/mo.
- On thin-margin verticals, reduction to sub-$500k/mo inference cost materially changes product economics and unlocks expansion.

Immediate asks / next steps (owners & dates)
- Jonas: deliver a 2-slide ROI summary and a 1-page pilot config (models/latency SLO, expected batch windows, cache policy) — due Wed, 5/7.
- Marissa: provide a pilot SOW and a simple cost model spreadsheet broken into hosted vs dedicated vs pilot credits (attachment: token_model_estimates.xlsx) — due Thu, 5/8.
- Hannah: confirm procurement timeline and sample PO terms; check whether CashLance needs an internal security questionnaire before signature — due Mon, 5/12.
- Asha: confirm budget ceiling and which channels (support vs onboarding) we should prioritize for the 3-month pilot.

Attachments referenced: pilot-sow-draft.pdf (placeholder), token_model_estimates.xlsx (we'll populate with scenarios).

If any of the levers above look off relative to your expectations, flag them and we'll adjust the pilot scope. Happy to run a short cost simulation on your real token mix if you can share anonymized logs.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0129

From: Asha Patel <asha@cashlance.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, CashLance Procurement <procurement@cashlance.com>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: spend runway, token-melt & batching hypotheses

Jonas — thanks, useful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Budget ceiling is firm at ~$60k/month for inference for the first 3 months of production; engineering can make tradeoffs if we can show measured savings.
- Priority: customer support assistant (70% traffic) then onboarding flows (30%).
- Timeline: procurement can move in ~2 weeks if we get an SOW + a short procurement-friendly PO draft.

Can you send a 1-page ROI with the pilot config (we want to present to finance on Friday). Also attaching a draft PO (attachment stub: purchase-order-draft.pdf) — not final, just our internal template.

If you can show an example where the combined levers deliver >=30% reduction in run-rate with minimal latency impact, we'll greenlight a 3-month pilot.

Asha
Head of Product 
CashLance
asha@cashlance.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: spend runway, token-melt & batching hypotheses

Thanks — adding a slightly more conservative set of numbers based on our standard pilot telemetry. Two quick notes for the ROI slide:
- Pilot sizing we recommend: 2x dedicated A100-equivalent nodes during peak windows, auto-scale to 3x for burst (we can simulate in-hosted before commit).
- Token assumptions: 1.2M tokens/day steady; 1.8M tokens/day peak (weekdays). We'll model three scenarios in the spreadsheet: conservative (25% savings), base (40% savings), optimistic (55% savings).

Preliminary cost math for the spreadsheet (conservative scenario):
- 36M tokens/mo * $0.032 (hosted baseline) = $1,152,000/mo baseline
- Expected drop 25% -> 27M tokens/mo equivalent
- Dedicated blended: assumed $0.024/token -> $648,000/mo (conservative)

I attached token_model_estimates.xlsx (summary table + sensitivity tabs). Marissa will finalize the SOW draft; Jonas, I'll drop the SOW into the shared link tonight.

Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Asha — looping in procurement details. A few operational points and a pilot offer: 
- Procurement: we can accept the CashLance PO template. Standard lead time for enterprise SOW + PO is ~7–10 business days once SOW is agreed.
- Pilot offer: Redwood can provide a 10% pilot credit for the first 90 days (applied to invoice) and a 90-day SLA commitment for availability/median latency (detailing to be included in the SOW).
- Security: if you need our SOC2 summary and data handling addendum, we'll send by EOD.

Next concrete asks
- Marissa: finalize SOW (include pilot credit language + SLOs) and post into DocuSign link by EOD 5/6.
- Jonas: prepare the 1-page ROI for Friday (5/9) to support Asha's finance review.
- Asha: confirm budget cap one more time and whether we should hard-limit to support channel only for month 1.

Thanks — Hannah
